expectation: Membrane rings on small, scattered lymphocytes (NK cells and a subset of CD8 T cells). Uncommon. They should sit in the lamina propria, in lymphoid aggregates or as single cells within the epithelium, not across the epithelium itself.
notes: NKG2A signal fills the whole epithelial mucosa and follows tissue texture and cell density. No distinct scattered lymphocytes stand out. This looks like background or autofluorescence, not a specific stain.
observed: A: broad yellow over the whole mucosal and epithelial layers, with linear streaks in the muscle and a rectangular stripe artefact. B and C: diffuse cytoplasmic haze over the epithelium and stroma, with no single positive cells. D: cells tinted alike, with no distinct membrane-ringed lymphocyte.
why: The signal follows the epithelial compartment and tissue density everywhere, with no distinct, sparse lymphocyte population, so there is no specific NKG2A staining.
